newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - CKI steps up for HK$3.8 bln.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - CKI steps up for HK$3.8 bln.

text.p: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) has invited banks to bid on a HK$3.8 billion five-year loan, bankers said on Monday.
CKI was not seeking debt financing, despite winning an A-minus long-term corproate credit rating last week they said. they said.
"Why did they get a rating if they're going to get a loan?" asked one, adding that the deal was definitely a loan structure.

No details are available on what the funds are earmarked for, but CKI said last week that it had agreed to pay 383 million yuan for a 66 percent stake in two sections of China's National Highway 107 linking north and south.
CKI also said it was in talks to invest in a number of other infrastructure projects in Henan province.
It has a total of 712 kilometres of roads in its China transport investment portfolio, representing a total road and bridge investment of about HK$5.8 billion.

Bank of China's floating-rate certificate of deposit attracted more than 40 banks to it, just short of the record number of participants attracted to the HK$8.2 billion loan by the Airport Authority early last year.

"It was an auspicious time," said one banker, referring to the deal's timing -- it was launched before Hong Kong was handed back to China's rule at midnight on June 30, and responses were due back on July 3.
"It's a show of support for the Bank of China," said the banker, who sold some paper at a profit on Monday morning.
In the secondary market, it was trading at about 33 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate, against an all-in yield to top level participants of 36 basis points.

In another oversubscribed China deal, Casil Clearing Investment BVI, an arm of China Aerospace International Holdings had its floating-rate note increased to US$150 million from the original issue size of US$40 million, bankers said.
The three-year deal has puts and calls in year two, and was priced at a par to float at 130 basis poiunts over the six- month London Interbank Offered Rate.
In other news, Hong Kong's Airport Authority is said to be under siege from banks wanting to put together a loan facility of about HK$4 billion with a five-year maturity.
Its last borrowing, the HK$8.2 billion loan which closed at the beginning of last year, was probably one of the year's most successful loan syndications.
However, the Airport Authority may still opt for debt.
It said recently that it was finalising a HK$5 billion note issuance facility with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), which would act as arranging agent for the facility.
The facility can be increased with the agreement of the HKMA, broadening the Airport Authority's funding options.
Cho Hung Bank has mandated SocGen Asia to arrange a US$100 million floating-rate note issue.
The one-year issue is likely to be done on a club deal basis, with talk of pricing in the mid 50s, bankers said.
Bakrie Indonesia BV has increased its floating-rate note to US$135 million from the original issue size of US$125 million, arranger Sumitomo Finance Asia said.
